name: Drorit Wertheim
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: David and Drorit Wertheim are the children of the late Moshe Wertheim (d. 2016) who founded the Central Bottling Company, Israel's only Coca Cola bottler.
Before he died, Moshe Wertheim gave his children ownership over the company, as well as his shares in Mizrahi Tefahot Bank and Alony Hetz.
In 2018, David purchased all of his sister's shares in Alony Hetz, then sold them because of Israeli anti-monopoly rules.
In 2019, the siblings became majority shareholders in Mizrahi Tefahot bank.
David controls 67% of the Central Bottling Company and manages the business while Drorit owns the remaining shares.

name: Fatih Tosyali
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2018-2019); Hurun Global (2020-2022)
forbes_bio: Along with his brothers Fuat and Ayhan, Fatih Tosyali presides over a steel and iron producer with 18 facilities in Turkey, Serbia and Algeria.
As a child, he joined his father and brothers in a small workshop in Iskenderun, where they made sheet metal out of used tin cheese cans.
From sheet metal, they went on to bucket and stove production. The family began investing in Algeria in 2008.
Including overseas operations, Tosyali Holding is on track to become Turkey's top iron and steel producer, with an 8.5 million ton capacity by 2019.
Fatih is on the board of Tosyali Holding and shares ownership in the business with his brothers, who are also billionaires.
forbes_facts: Fatih Tosyali is the Honorary Consul for Slovenia.
By the end of 2019, Tosyali Holding expects to have invested in excess of $6 billion in integrated production facilities located in Oran, Algeria.

name: Alan Zekelman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Alan Zekelman owns a stake in his family's steel business, Zekelman Industries.
The $3.3 billion (revenues) company is one of North America's largest steel pipe and tube makers.
The company has also pumped more than $1 billion into Z Modular, a division that is developing modular apartment complexes in places such as Texas, Arizona and Canada.
Alan and his brothers, fellow billionaires Barry Zekelman and Clayton Zekelman, split 100% ownership of Zekelman Industries.
They sold the company to the Carlyle Group in 2006 for some $1.2 billion, but bought the business back in 2011.
forbes_facts: One of Zekelman Industries' subsidiaries, Atlas Tube, produced steel for stretches of the Mexican border wall in Arizona.

name: Donald Friese
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Donald Friese's fortune stems from C.R. Laurence, which manufactures or distributes more than 65,000 products for the glass industry.
In 2015 he sold C.R. Laurence to a big customer, Oldcastle BuildingEnvelope, a subsidiary of Irish conglomerate CRH, for $1.3 billion in cash.
Friese grew up a poor orphan in rural Pennsylvania, going to work on a dairy farm at age 12 before enlisting in the Army after high school.
After a three-year tour, he moved to California with just $125 and landed in the warehouse of C.R. Laurence, then a small distributor of supplies.
He climbed the ladder, amassing equity in the company until he owned 100%, and expanded by purchasing competitors and moving into manufacturing.
forbes_facts: When Friese sold C.R. Laurence, he gave his employees $85 million. All 1,600 longtime workers got a bonus check -- some for more than $1 million.
Since he retired in 2018, Friese has been focusing on philanthropy through his family foundation. He has so far donated at least $60 million to the organization.

name: Magic Johnson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Earvin "Magic" Johnson is one of the greatest NBA players of all time. Forbes named him a billionaire in October 2023.
Johnson earned only around $40 million total as a Los Angeles Lakers player, mainly in the 1980s, and even at his peak only brought in between $2 million and $4 million per year in endorsements.
Instead he built his wealth through joint venture partnerships in everything from movie theaters, Starbucks franchises, real estate and healthcare.

The majority of his fortune comes from a 60% ownership stake in life insurance company Equitrust, which has grown from $16 billion in assets under management to $33 billion since he took over in 2015.
He also owns small ownership stakes in the NFL's Washington Commanders, MLB's Los Angeles Dodgers, WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks and MLS' LAFC.
forbes_facts: Johnson is just the fourth athlete billionaire Forbes has ever identified. The others are Michael Jordan, Tiger Woods and LeBron James.
Before the 1979 NBA Draft, Nike offered Johnson stock in the company and royalties on shoe sales. He declined in favor of $100,000 per year cash from Converse.

name: Nikolay Fartushnyak
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Nikolay Fartushnyak, along with his older brother Vladimir and Alexander Mikhalskiy, cofounded Russia's largest sports and fashion retailer Sportmaster.
The Fartushnyak brothers and Mikhalskiy are also cofounders of Ostin, a Russian fast-fashion retailer.
In 2014 Fartushnyak and Igor Khudokormov, known as the "Russian sugar king," bought Swedish company Agrokultura, which owns about 200,000 hectares of agricultural land in Russia.
Fartushnyak and his partners started out with distribution business in the early 1990s and supplied French consumer goods to their home market.
His Sportmaster also has its own brands, such as Demix, which makes sports goods, apparel and shoes.

name: Blairo Maggi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2024); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Blairo Maggi is the son of Andre Maggi and Lucia Maggi, cofounders of Brazil's Andre Maggi Group.
Amaggi is one of Brazil's largest producers of soybeans and other commodities.
He took over as the chief executive of Amaggi after his father's death in 2001. Although he no longer holds the position, he remains a controlling shareholder.
Maggi has previously served as Brazil's minister of agriculture and the governor of the state of Mato Grasso.
forbes_facts: Maggi was referred to as the "King of Soy" by Brazilian media during his time leading the business.
Amaggi produces approximately 1.2 million tons of soy, corn, and cotton in Brazil each year.

name: Cristiano Ronaldo
name_chinese: 克里斯蒂亚诺·罗纳尔多
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Cristiano Ronaldo is arguably the world's most popular athlete, with nearly 1 billion followers on Instagram, Facebook and X.
The Portuguese soccer star played for Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus before signing with Saudi club Al-Nassr in 2023.
Al-Nassr pays Ronaldo more than $200 million annually, helping make him the world's highest-paid athlete for four consecutive years.
Ronaldo had a record 973 career goals as of the start of the 2026 World Cup. He wants to be the first to reach 1,000 before he retires.
Ronaldo is the first active athlete to surpass $2 billion in career earnings on and off the field before taxes and agents' fees.
